Aberrant conduction

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient has intermittent early beats during monitoring. Each begins with a premature abnormal P wave, but some are followed by a broad QRS with a bundle-branch pattern. Which mechanism can explain the widened ventricular complex without requiring a ventricular ectopic origin?

  1. A sinus impulse delayed until after ventricular repolarization
  2. Persistent ventricular fibrillation
  3. Isolated failure of the pulse oximeter
  4. An atrial premature impulse reaching a refractory bundle branch
  5. Complete cessation of atrial depolarization
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

An atrial premature impulse reaching a refractory bundle branch

A PAC can conduct aberrantly when part of the His-Purkinje system remains refractory.

Understanding the options

An atrial premature impulse reaching a refractory bundle branch
A PAC can conduct aberrantly when part of the His-Purkinje system remains refractory.
Complete cessation of atrial depolarization
The visible early P wave demonstrates atrial depolarization.
A sinus impulse delayed until after ventricular repolarization
The beat is early, not delayed.
Persistent ventricular fibrillation
Fibrillation does not yield discrete conducted complexes.
Isolated failure of the pulse oximeter
A pulse oximeter issue does not change the ECG QRS morphology.
